context: You help out in a local school's English class. The kids are curious, and the teachers expect polite Japanese.

phrases.jp: よろしくお{願|ねが}いします。
phrases.en: Nice to be working with you.
phrases.note: Say it to the teachers in the staff room on day one.

phrases.jp: {先生|せんせい}、ちょっといいですか。
phrases.en: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

phrases.jp: {名前|なまえ}は{何|なん}ですか。
{黒板|こくばん}に{書|か}いてもいいですか。
phrases.en: May I write on the blackboard?

phrases.jp: すごいね！よくできたね！
phrases.note: Praise for kids. Speak casually with children.

dialogue_setting: In a primary school classroom, before the lesson starts.

dialogue.speaker: Student
dialogue.jp: {先生|せんせい}、どこから{来|き}たの？

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: スペインから{来|き}たよ。どこにあるか{知|し}ってる？
dialogue.en: I'm from Spain. Do you know where it is?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: じゃあ、{地図|ちず}で{見|み}てみよう。
dialogue.en: Then let's look at the map.

dialogue.speaker: Teacher
dialogue.jp: みんな、{席|せき}に{着|つ}いてください。

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: {先生|せんせい}、{次|つぎ}は{何|なに}をしましょうか。

kanji.where: Above the teachers' room door in every school. Knock, open, and say {失礼|しつれい}します as you go in.
kanji.related: Related: {校長室|こうちょうしつ} principal's office.

tip.title: 失礼します opens every door
tip.body: When you enter a staff room or office, say {失礼|しつれい}します; when you leave, {失礼|しつれい}しました. Students will call you {先生|せんせい} even as a volunteer. Casual with kids, always です/ます with teachers.

challenge.prompt: After class, ask the teacher: "What should I prepare for tomorrow?"
challenge.hint: prepare = {準備|じゅんび}する, + ～ばいいですか
challenge.model_answer: {明日|あした}は{何|なに}を{準備|じゅんび}すればいいですか。
